SM Enamul Hoque, Deputy Attorney-General---For the Appellant. 
Zahidul Bari, Advocate---For Respondent No. 7 
Md Hossain with Tapan Kumar Bepari, Advocates---For Respondent No. 1.
parties:
Bangladesh ------ Appellant
Vs 
Serajul Haque and others ------ Respondents
full_judgment:
Siddiqur Rahman Miah J: This appeal at the instance of the plaintiff-government is directed against the judgment and decree dated 7-9-1994 passed by the learned Subordinate Judge, 2nd Court, Gazipur in Title Suit No. 31 of 1994 dismissed the suit.

2. The appellant as plaintiff instituted the suit in the Court of learned Subordinate Judge, 2nd Court, Gazipur, for declaring the judgment and decree dated 7-9-1994 as null and void and for declaration of title in respect of the suit land.

3. The case of the plaintiff, in short, is that the suit land originally belonged to Zaminder of Sree Faltani and to the waqf estate of Baliyadi Zaminder; that the then British government acquired the suit land measuring 125 acres including other land of this area for certain period for converting this area as government forest land by notification No. 1139 dated 14-11-1951 after serving notice upon the Zaminder and local people on 11-8-1951; that SA and RS khatian were correctly prepared in the names of the government and the forest department; that again, the suit land was permanently acquired by the government vide notification No. 4836 LR and No. 4849 LR dated 2-4-1956 and thus the suit land was permanently vested in the government and forest department annulling all the rights of the Zaminder therein and that the suit land has already been in the control and possession of the government as per notification No. XII / Forest 13-19 /85 /19 dated 31-3-1985 under section 4 of the Forest Act. It is further contended that the suit land has been entered into the Khatian of Forest Department; that the office of Divisional Forest Officer is located at Moakhali that there is no office of Forest Department at Kaliakore; that in order to suppress the summons, the address of the Divisional Forest Officer was shown at Kaliakore; that summons was not served upon the Divisional Forest Officer in Title Suit No. 329 of 1974; that suppressing the summons collusively and on practising fraud upon the Court, the defendants illegally obtained ex parte decree on 4-12-1975 and that the defendants in order to grab the forest land created some forged papers. It is further stated that the appearance of the Government pleader and filing of written statement was fraudulently shown; that the suit land was all along in the possession of Forest Department; that the defendants have no right, title and possession in the suit land; that knowing about the ex prrte decree in title Suit No.329 of 1974 on 4-12-1975 from Misc. case No. 4 of 1968 of ADC (Rev), Gazipur, the plaintiff filed the suit for declaration of the ex parte decree void and for declaration of title in respect of the suit land.

4. The defendant Nos. 1 to 6, 7 and 8 filed written statements, inter alia, denying the material allegations contained in the plaint.

5. The case of the defendant Nos.1 to 6, in short, is that the suit land belonged to the khas possession of then Zaminder Babu Khamata Kinkar Roy of Showapur, PS Dhamria whose interest was that of a tenure holder in respect of the suit property and his name was recorded as such in the CS khatian and in the relevant registers and that while having such tenure interest, the said Zaminder by an unregistered amalnama dated 15th Poush 1344 BS settled the suit land to Md Abdul Gafur, who took physical possession of the said land after obtaining such allotment and since then they have been possessing the land by annually selling the jungles to the buyers who took the same for cutting and taking away the shrubs and trees for use as fuel. It is further contended that Abdul Gafur died leaving 6 sons namely, Serajul Islam, Furat Ali, Abdul Balek, Noya Miah, Chanda Lai and Elihi Box; that the heirs of Abdul Gafur were also in possession of suit land; that Serajul Islam and the other heirs of Serajul Islam filed Title Suit No. 329 of 1974 against the Department of Forest for permanent injunction restraining them from disturbing their peaceful possession; that summons of that suit was properly served; that the learned Government pleader appeared and filed written statement but lastly, he did not turn up and ultimately the suit was decreed ex parte on 4-12-1975.

6. It is also contended that the plaintiffs executed and registered a power of attorney to sell and manage the suit property in favour of Md Ahasan and his wife, Ayatennessa, who by virtue of that power of attorney sold 2.15½ acres of land in favour Gulsanwara; that again Ashan and his wife, Ayatennessa, sold the rest 21.51½ acres of land to Gulshanwara who has been possessing land in question and that the Forest Department has no title and possession in the suit land and that the defendant has filed the suit in order to harass the plaintiffs.

7. The case of defendant No. 7, in short, is that the suit land originally belonged. to Babu Khamata Kinkar Roy who leased out the suit land to Abdul Gafur; that CS record was prepared in the name of Abdul Gafur; that Abdul Gafur died leaving 6 sons who filed Title Suit No. 329 of 1974 and the suit was decreed ex parte.

8. It is further contended that heirs of Abdul Gafur executed a Power of Attorney in favour of Md Ashan and his wife, Ayatennessa, to sell and manage the suit land; that power of attorney holder Ashan and his wife, Ayatennessa; sold 7.31 acres of land by a registered kabala dated 19-9-1989 in favour of this defendant who has been possessing the suit land after mutating his name; that the suit land was not acquired by the government; that no notice of acquisition was served upon the defendant Nos. 1 to 6 and other interested persons; that the acquisition is illegal and ineffective and that the plaintiff has no title and possession in the suit land and, as such, the suit is liable to be set aside.

9. The defendant No. 8 also filed a separate written statement, inter alia, contending that Abdul Gafur acquiring the suit land by way of amalnama died leaving defendant Nos. 1 to 6; that defendant Nos. 1 to 6 filed Title Suit No. 329 of 1974 for permanent injunction and obtained ex parte decree; that the defendant Nos. 1 to 6 having title and possession executed and registered a power of attorney on 15-12-1977 in favour of Md Ashan and his wife Ayatennessa who transferred 21.511/2 acres of land in favour of this defendant; that the boundary of his land was measured by an employee of ADC (Rev.), Gazipur; that getting possession he constructed but thereon and possessed other land through bargader.

10. At the trial, the plaintiff examined 1 (one) witness and the defendant No.7 examined himself as DW 1.

11. The plaintiff filed two Gazette Notifications dated 14th November, 1951 and 31st March, 1985 which were taken into deposition but erroneously were not marked as exhibits. The plaintiff also filed LR No. 4836 and 4849 dated 2-4-1956 in support of his contention.

12. On the other hand, the defendant No. 7 only contested the suit and filed Zamindari Pattannama, some Zamindari Dhakhilas, some government Dhakhilas, CS khatian and certified copies of SA khatians which have been exhibited under different marks.

13. The learned Subordinate Judge framed the following issues on the pleading of the parties:

1. It the suit maintainable in its present form?

2. Have the defendant Nos. 1 to 6 obtained ex parte judgment and decree in Title Suit No. 329 of 1974 from the 2nd Court of Munsif, Dhaka collusively beyond the knowledge of the plaintiff?

3. Has the plaintiff right, title, interest and possession in the suit land?

4. Is the plaintiff entitled to get decree as prayed for?

5. To what relief, if any, is the plaintiff entitled to get.

14. The learned Subordinate Judge disbelieving the case of the plaintiff dismissed the suit by his judgment and decree dated 7-9-1994.

15. Being aggrieved by the aforesaid judgment and decree dated 7-9-1994, the plaintiff preferred the appeal before this Court.

16. Mr SM Enamul Hoque, the learned Deputy Attorney-General, has placed before us the plaint, w7itten statement, deposition and documents of the parties and the impugned judgment.

17. He further submits that the suit property were vested absolutely in the hand of the Government as "forest land" by a gazette notification No. 1139 dated 14-11-51 after serving the notice upon the Zaminder on 11-8-1951 and the local people on 11-8-1951; that moreover, the SA khatian and RS khatian were correctly prepared in the name of the Government and the Forest Department; that the suit property cannot be settled by anyone to anybody; that the plaintiff of the present suit was not made party as defendant in the earlier title suit No. 329 of 1974; that the present defendant as plaintiffs collusively made wrong persons as defendants in that earlier suit and that managed false signatures in summons notice and collusively obtained fraudulent decree suppressing summons. He further submits that the plaintiff came to know about the ex parte decree of earlier suit after getting notice against the Miscellaneous Case No. 4 of 1988 in the Court of the Additional Deputy Commissioner (Rev.) on 5-7-1988; that no pattan was given by Zaminder to Abdul Gafur and that the rent receipts and khatians were manufactured and that the finding and decision both are erroneous in law as well as on fact, as such, the same is liable to be set aside.

18. Mr Zahidul Bari, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the defendant No. 7, submits that the suit land originally belonged to Zaminder Babu Khamata Kinkor Roy who leased out the suit land to Abdul Gafur; that CS and SA record were prepared in the name of Abdul Gafur; that Abdul Gafur died. leaving 6 sons who executed and registered the power of attorney in favour of Ashan and his wife, Ayatennessa, to sell and manage the property and that by virtue of that power of attorney Ashan and his wife, Ayatennessa, sold 7.31 acres of land by registered kabala deed dated 19-9-1989 in favour of this defendant No. 7 who have been possessing the land and mutated his name. He further submits that the suit was not acquired by the government; that no notice of acquisition was served by the defendant Nos. 1 to 6 and other interested persons; that the acquisition is illegal and ineffective and that the government has no right, title and interest in the suit land. He further submits that the learned Subordinate Judge, 2nd Court, Gazipur, was quite justified in passing the impugned judgment and thus he committed no illegality in passing the impugned judgment which does not call for any interference. He further submits that the suit is barred by limitation and the suit was not preferred by proper person, as such, the appeal is liable to be dismissed.

19. Mr Mohammad Hossain, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the respondent No. 1, submits that the suit land belonged to Zaminder Babu Khamata Kinkor Roy who settled the suit land to Abdul Gafur; that CS and SA record was correctly preferred in his name; that Abdul Gafur died leaving behind 6 sons who have right, title and interest in the suit land and who executed the power of attorney in favour of Ashan and his wife, Ayatennessa, who also sold the suit land to different persons and they are in possession; that the suit is hit by section 42 of the Specific Relief Act as the plaintiff has not prayed for consequential relief and that the suit is barred by limitation. He further submits that the judgment and decree passed by the learned Subordinate Judge does not suffer from any legality and legal infirmity which must not be upheld and the appeal is liable to be dismissed.

20. The point for determination is whether the learned Subordinate Judge was justified in passing the impugned judgment and decree dated 7-9-1994.

The plaintiff government filed this case for two reliefs: one, for declaring the judgment of Title Suit No. 329 of 1974 as null and void and secondly, for declaration of title in respect of the suit land.

21. In respect of the first relief, the contention of the plaintiff appellant is that the summons of Title Suit No. 329 of 1974 was not served at all and that plaintiff of that suit suppressing the summons and manufacturing some false papers obtained a fraudulent decree practising fraud upon the Court.

22. In the context of present circumstances of the case, the defendants-respondents are to prove that the summons of Title Suit No. 329 of 1974 were properly served and the documents filed by them were genuine. The well settled provision of law is that due service of summons is the essential pre-requisite of an ex parte decree. The question of due service of summons upon the defendant in Title Suit No. 329 of 1974 is a matter of supreme importance for keeping the ex parte decree valid. The service of summons is stoutly denied by the plaintiff. The learned Subordinate Judge based his decision upon mere surmise and conjecture without ascertaining the vital question of due service of summons with reference to the evidence on record and the law bearing on the subject.

23. The defendants-respondents have totally failed to show whether the summons was duly served upon the defendant of Title Suit No. 329 of 1974 either by process server or by registered post. The plaintiff of the Title Suit No. 329 of 1974 did not examine the process server in order to prove the service of summons nor did plaintiff file any paper to show that the summons through registered post was served. On the other hand, PW 1 Md Hafizur Rahman, Bit Officer of Forest Department, stoutly deposed that forest department got the suit land by Gazette notifications marked exhibit No. 1 series; that SA and RS record was prepared in the name of Forest Department; that they were not aware of the ex parte decree dated 4-12-1975 as the summons of Title Suit No. 329 of 1974 was collusively suppressed showing the address of Divisional Forest Officer at Kaliakore. He further stoutly deposed that there is no Divisional Forest Office at Kaliakore; that their Divisional Office is located at Mohakhali, Dhaka, and that the forest department has incurred irreparable loss due to the ex parte decree dated 4-12-1975.

24. The defendant No. 7 who was the subsequent purchaser of a small portion of the suit land was examined on the side of defendant. The plaintiff of Title Suit No. 329 of 1974 has not come to depose. So this witness had no knowledge about that suit as he purchased his portion of suit land long after the ex parte decree dated 4-12-1975. This witness frankly confesses that he was not party in title Suit No. 329 of 1974; that he cannot say how the plaintiffs of the case obtained the ex parte decree and that he did not see the summons of that suit.

25. It appears from the plaint of title Suit No. 329 of 1974 that the address of the Divisional Forest Office was shown as "Divisional Forest office, Kaliakore." It appears from evidence that there is no forest office at Kaliakore. Thus it is clearly evident from evidence that the summons of Title Suit No. 329 of 1974 was collusively suppressed showing the wrong address of the Divisional Forest Office.

26. The defendants-respondents claim that the learned Government pleader appeared and filed written statement in that suit. But the plaintiff-appellant categorically denies such assertion. The defendants respondents failed to file any scrap of paper or adduce any evidence to show that the learned Government pleader appeared and filed written statement in that case. This assertion of the defendants-respondents has fallen flat without any evidence. Before decreeing the suit ex parte, the Court must be satisfied as to the proof of service of summons upon the defendants and the claim of the plaintiff by cogent evidence. An ex parte decree may be set aside on either of the two grounds i.e. non-service of summons on the defendants or the defendants were prevented by sufficient cause from appearing before the Court when the suit was taken up for hearing.

<u>27. From the materials on record, it becomes manifestly clear that summons upon the defendants were not at all served or there is nothing on record to show that the government appeared and contested that suit. Thus it is evident that the defendant was prevented by sufficient cause from appearing before the Court when the suit No. 329 of 1974 was called on for hearing. Moreover, it is worthy to state that when the elements of fraud and collusion is manifested in procuring the ex parte decree, that decree vitiates.</u>

28. The proposition of law emerging out of the authorities is that in ex parte disposal of the suit, the Court is required to observe minimum legal requirement and the order should show application of the Court's judicial mind as to whether the plaintiff's witnesses and other papers produced proved the plaintiff's case. The duty of a Court is to administer justice in accordance with law, Courts are required not to exercise punitive jurisdiction by depriving defendant. Our law of procedure is also designed to facilitate justice. The laws of procedure are grounded on the principle that a litigant public and a citizen should not be condemned unheard and decision should not be reached behind his back. The proceedings that affect his properties should be heard in his presence. The Court possesses a discretion to undo injustice caused to the citizens of the state and the Court must exercise that discretion. The hands of the Court are not tied by the ex parte orders. Mandate of law is that interference must be called for in a case like this. In this context, it is significant to point out that in furtherance of the ends of justice Court always leans in favour of setting aside an ex parte decree/order, rather than maintain the same because Court exists for the advancement of justice not to deprive a litigant of his right.

29. In the light of the above facts and circumstances of the case, evidence on record and law bearing on the subject, we are of the view that ex party decree dated 4-12-1975 is liable to be set aside.

30. Now we turn to the second point, as to whether the present plaintiff-appellant has succeeded to prove the case.

<u>31. Both the plaintiff-appellant and defendants respondents claim title and possession in the suit land.</u>

<u>32. It is admitted that nature of land is forest. The defendants claim the suit land on the basis of amalnama dated 15th Poush, 1344 BS taken by Abdul Gafur; that Zaminder granted Dakhilas; that RS and SA record were prepared in the name of Abdul Gafur and that Abdul Gafur paid rent to the government.</u>

<u>33. The learned Deputy Attorney-General stoutly submits that the amalnamas, Dakhalias and rent receipts are false and fabricated. In support of his contention, he firstly argues that the heirs of Abdul Gafur did contest the suit; that they have not been adduced as witness; that subsequent purchaser, defendant No. 7, Habibur Rahman, only deposed that he was not party in Title Suit No. 329 of 1974; that he cannot say how the plaintiff got the suit land and that the DW 1 is not a proper witness. His second submission is that the plaintiffs of Title Suit No. 329 of 1974 have failed to prove their title and possession in the suit land and the plaintiff of that suit have not taken any step to contest the suit filed by the government. He lastly submits that the amalnama alleged to have been granted by Zaminder on the 15th Poush, 1344 BS corresponding to sometime in the year 1938 BS; that CS record was finally published in between 1919 and 1921; that CS record which was finally published long before 1938 AD and thus the appearance of the name of Abdul Gafur in CS Khatian, who alleged to have taken settlement some time in 1938 AD, have been proved to be fabricated and manufactured one. Moreover, the amalnama has not been proved as per law.</u>

<u>34. We find substance in the submission of the learned Deputy Attorney-General. Since the foundation of Title of the defendants-respondents has not been proved and thus the CS khatian has been proved fabricated and manufactured and the SA khatian prepared on the basis of alleged CS khatian has no leg to stand. Dhakalias granted on the basis of khatian does not create any title which was also obtained fraudulently.</u>

35. On the other hand, the definite case of the plaintiff is that the government acquired the suit land measuring 125 acres and other land by Gazette notification No. 11397 dated 14th November, 1951 and subsequent notification No. XIII-13-19/85 /219 dated 31st March, 1985. The Bit officer of Khaliajani Bit as PW 1 in support of the above fact deposed that the suit land was entered into gazette marked exhibit-1 series; that the Forest Department has been possessing the suit land since 1951 and that RS and SA record was prepared in the name of Forest Department.

In view of the above documentary and oral evidence, we are of the view that the title and possession of the plaintiff government have been proved beyond reasonable doubt.

36. Moreover, the law relating to the retention of khas land in the possession of tenant is envisaged in the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act 1951.

<u>37. Section 43 of the Act provides for publishing a notification declaring that compensation assessment roll in respect of any village or group of villages or local area has been finally published. Sub-section (3) of section 44 of the Act provides that all interests of raiyats etc. in non-retainable khas land other than the interest which has already been acquired under any other provision of the Act i.e. section 3 under Chapter II or sub-section 3 of section 46E shall be deemed to have been acquired by the government and vest absolutely in the government free from all encumbrances from the first day of the agricultural year next following the date of publication in the official Gazette. On the other hand, sub-section 1 of the said section 44 provides that all interest of rent receivers in the estates, tenures and all other rent receiving interests in any holding or tenancy or in the non-retainable khas land other than the interest already acquired under Chapter-II or sub-section 3 of section 46E shall be deemed to have been acquired by the government and vest absolutely in the government from the first day of the agricultural year next following the date of publication of such notification in the official gazette. Thus, reading of section 20, 43, and 44 of the Act together, we have no option but to hold that non-retainable khas land belonging either to the rent receiver or to the tenant shall be deemed to have been acquired by the Government and vested in the government with the publication of a notification about final publication of the compensation assessment roll in the official gazette from the first day of the agricultural year next following the date of publication of such notification.</u>

38. Sub-section (1) of section 20 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act provides that "on the acquisition of interest of rent receivers in any area under Chapter V, no rent receiver, cultivating raiyat, cultivating under-raiyat of non-agricultural tenant shall be entitled to retain possession of any of his khas lands in such area except as provided in sub-section,(2)."

39. Under sub-section (2) of section 20 of the said Act, persons mentioned in sub-section (1) above are entitled to retain possession of one hundred (now sixty) standard bighas of land as tenant under the government. Now there is no scope for retaining possession of non-retainable Khas land by any tenant in Bangladesh on any ground whatsoever.

<u>40. In the facts and circumstance of the case and evidence on record, we are inclined to hold that the defendants-respondents obtained the ex parte decree in Title Suit No. 329 of 1974 suppressing summons collusively and practising fraud upon the Court. Again, the defendants-respondents manufacturing some false and concocted amalnama dhakhilas and khatians tried to validate the evil design of grabbing huge quantum of the forest khas land practising fraud upon the Court and their evil design has been revealed in the appeal. The essence of law being to advance the cause of justice and not to frustrate it. If fraud is allowed to be perpetratect and perpetuated the sanctity attached to law will wither away with disastrous consequences to the society. The case of the defendants-respondents is the glaring example of committing fraud upon the Court which cannot be encouraged.</u>

41. In view of the foregoing discussion and the law bearing on the subject, we find that the learned Subordinate Judge erred in law as well as on fact in passing the ex parte decree dated 7-9-1994 in Title Suit No. 329 of 1974 and also in dismissing the suit under challenge.

42. We find merit in the appeal.

43. In the result, the appeal is allowed without any order as to costs and the judgment and decree dated 4-12-1975 passed by the learned Munsif, 2nd Court, Dhaka Judge in Title suit No. 329 of 1974 is illegal, invalid and collusive, null and void which is not binding upon the plaintiff-appellant and the suit is decreed declaring plaintiff's title in the suit land.

Send down the LCR at once.

End.
